## Sharing cake {#ss7-cake .lim-lesson .lim-cake-slide}

Mr Greasley shares a cake equally with his two favourite (but greedy) students.

They ask for more, so he divides **his remaining piece into thirds** again, giving one piece to each student.

<div class="lim-cake" data-module="cake-sharing"></div>

::: notes

Use the physical cake alongside the model. Share again makes one equal three-way split of the teacher’s current share. Initially the whole cake belongs to Mr Greasley. Ask students to predict before every cut. The single bar always represents one whole cake at a fixed scale. Under it, Student 1 and Student 2 each have a colour-matched running sum that retains every individual piece and equals their current total. For example, after round 3 each row shows 1/3+1/9+1/27=13/27. A separate row shows Mr Greasley’s remaining fraction, 1/27. All values update immediately and stay visible. Up to six rounds are shown at their exact proportions. Round n gives each student 1/3^n extra, total (1−3^(−n))/2, and leaves the teacher 3^(−n). Reset returns to the whole cake, with each student at 0 and Mr Greasley at 1. State persists through slide navigation. Source: teacher’s Geometric Limiting Sum.pptx slides 4–5.

:::
